attempts.label: DANDI:001836
attempts.paper_title: Naturalistic behavior and self-generated neural activity predictive of self-correction
attempts.entry_title: Change-of-mind behavior in the spatial sequence task (Gu et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most behavioral findings held: rats learned the sequence, started biased toward side switching, corrected course on change-of-mind trials to the level of run-through trials, and showed fewer ripples during change of mind. The fall in switch bias held only in part (final ratio 1.85, not about 1.5), and the drop in switching on final choices was significant in fewer rats than reported. Distant decoded content was stronger after stopping than before in most rats, but its excess over inbound runs did not hold, and the files do not say which decoder made those tables. Links of remote and local extended content to correct next choices could not be tested because the decoder output is not deposited. Trial counts fell short because the dandiset holds fewer trials.
attempts.description: Tests the behavioral findings of Gu, Liu, Gillespie, Nevers, Denovellis, Coulter, Kay and Frank (2026) on dandiset 001836, which holds the recordings of five rats learning a hidden four-arm sequence. It builds trials from the well pokes and pumps, detects change-of-mind trials on the deposited linearized position, and tests learning, side-switching bias, trial counts and the corrective effect of changes of mind. It reads the paper's triggered decode tables for the Figure 3 claims and detects ripples on the LFP for Figure S7B; the other claims on hippocampal content need the decoder output, which the dandiset does not hold.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Gu et al. (2026) from dandiset 001836

outcomes.notes: Per day, the fraction of adjacent-trial transitions that are transitions of the rat's rewarded cycle (sessions with at least 20 trials) rises from 0.268, 0.338, 0.312, 0.416 and 0.408 on the first day to 0.511, 0.629, 0.598, 0.581 and 0.537 on the peak day for rats M, E, J, K and L, all above 0.25. The Spearman correlations with day are 1.00, 0.97, 0.72, 0.67 and 0.77, all positive (p = 0.071 and 0.072 for K and L; the criterion asks only for a positive sign). The peak day is every rat's last day in the dandiset. The dandiset holds 5, 9, 12, 8 and 6 days, against about 6, 9, 11, 8 and 6 in Figure 1C. The rats almost never repeat an arm (52 of 14708 transitions), so chance without repeats is 1/3, not the 25% of the paper and the criterion; the first day is above 1/3 in 3 rats (E, K, L) and the peak day in all 5.
deviations: The rat's cycle is read from the reward log (claims file, opening comment); a reward is followed by a reward at the cycle's next arm in 96 to 100% of cases, and trials are rewarded exactly when the final arm is the cycle's next arm after the last reward in 99.96% of the 14627 trials where that arm is defined.

Trials are built from the digital poke and pump events of the raw files (Methods, Behavioral analysis), a trial running from a home reward to the next outer poke. Against the Statescript logs of rats E, J, K and L the rewarded trials and the trials differ by at most one per session. Rat M's logs hold no counts to compare.

outcomes.notes: Values are reading a-i (10 cm, all trials), the first the criterion lists. Trials are 2083, 3519, 4578, 2959 and 1816 for M, E, J, K and L against 2370, 3554, 4628, 3779 and 2087; COM trials are 120, 196, 126, 226 and 240 against 107, 225, 138, 315 and 309. Within tolerance are 3 of 10 counts under readings a-i and a-ii, and 4 of 10 under b-i and b-ii (0.1 of the 96 cm arm, 9.6 cm; COM 120, 206, 128, 231 and 242), against the 8 the criterion asks for (5 for a partial reproduction). Every rat has at least 120 COM trials under every reading, so the "hundreds of COM trials per subject" part holds in the sense of the criterion. The dandiset holds 0.88, 0.99, 0.99, 0.78 and 0.87 of the paper's trials; the COM share of trials is 0.058, 0.056, 0.028, 0.076 and 0.132 against the paper's 0.045, 0.063, 0.030, 0.083 and 0.148, so for rats K and L most of the shortfall in COM trials follows the shortfall in trials. Per day, rat M has 5 days of 400 to 480 trials against the 6 days the paper reports, which would account for its shortfall; rats K and L have the 8 and 6 days of Figure 1C (319 to 456 trials a day for K, 265 to 337 for L), and no epoch is tagged other than "Session" or "Sleep", so where their missing trials are cannot be told from the files.
deviations: COM detection on the deposited 500 Hz linearization (Methods, Change of mind time detection), whose outer arms are 85.3 to 87.2 cm long in its units, against the 96 cm of the Methods; the 0.1-of-arm reading uses 0.1 of 96 cm (Methods, Behavioral apparatus, "The distance from the beginning of the arm to the end of the reward station is 96 cm"). The binary closing of the reversal mask uses scipy's default structure, as the Methods name the function without parameters.
The claims file's code reading that requires 0.8 s of position in the second before the reversal is applied; the 500 Hz linearization has at most 8% NaN samples in any epoch.

outcomes.notes: On the first analysed day P(switch-side)/P(same-side) is 5.53, 4.23, 3.76, 2.31 and 2.25 for rats M, E, J, K and L; the mean of the first two days is 5.59, 3.54, 4.00, 2.66 and 2.30. Both readings put all five above 2 (one-sided binomial p = 0.031). Transitions to the same arm (52 of 14708) are neither switch-side nor same-side and are left out.
deviations: Transitions between two trials to the same arm are left out, as they are neither kind; the claims file does not say.

outcomes.notes: The logistic regression over 14656 transitions gives a day effect of 0.933 (95% CI 0.920 to 0.946, p = 2.3e-23), within 0.92 plus or minus 0.092, the same with the day counted from the first or from the last day and with or without an intercept. The ratio on the peak day is 1.85 as a mean over rats (1.69, 1.94, 1.88, 1.84 and 1.89 for M, E, J, K and L) and 1.84 pooled, both outside 1.5 plus or minus 0.15. Fitted per rat, the day effect is significant in M, E, J and L and not in K (0.984, p = 0.38).
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out, as for fig1c-learning; the claims file does not say whether this claim uses the same selection.

outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. With the 10 cm threshold, the share of COM trials with one COM event is 0.875, 0.923, 0.960, 0.888 and 0.891 for M, E, J, K and L, and 15, 15, 5, 25 and 26 trials have two or more events (up to 5 in rat K). Trials with two or more COM arms, more than two arms entered, occur in every rat (14, 15, 5, 24 and 26). The 9.6 cm threshold gives the same outcome.
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.notes: Daily medians of the probability that the initial choice would have been rewarded are 0.18, 0.18, 0.00, 0.14 and 0.09 for M, E, J, K and L, and of the final choice being rewarded 0.47, 0.55, 0.72, 0.57 and 0.66; rank-sum p = 0.028, 0.0004, below 1e-4, 0.0008 and 0.0039. The paper reports p < 0.01 for M, J, K and L and p < 0.05 for E; here M is the rat at p < 0.05 only. Two COM trials, first in their session before any reward, have no correct arm and are left out. The 0.1-of-arm threshold (9.6 cm) gives the same outcome. Sessions with at least 20 trials (221 COM trials of rat K).
deviations: Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. Over 100 draws of nearby non-COM trials, each rat's median rank-sum p is 0.60, 0.57, 0.22, 0.17 and 0.75 for M, E, J, K and L at 10 cm (0.68, 0.52, 0.20, 0.16 and 0.75 at 9.6 cm); the share of draws with p < 0.05 is at most 0.22 (rat K). The median differences of daily reward rate, COM minus nearby, are -0.03, -0.08, 0.12, 0.05 and 0.00. Every COM trial had an eligible nearby trial. Each rat has 5 to 12 daily values, so the test has little power and the result is an absence of evidence.
deviations: Nearby trials are drawn within the same session; the Methods (Identification of nearby trials) say only within plus or minus 3 trials. The random draws use a fixed seed.
Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. The mean daily initial ratio exceeds the final in all five rats (medians 3.00 to 3.63 against 0.93 to 1.41), but the paired t-test reaches p < 0.01 only in rats J and K (p = 0.0023 and 0.0045 at 10 cm); E and L have p = 0.013 and 0.014 and M p = 0.42. The 9.6 cm threshold gives the same count (J 0.0022, K 0.0001, E 0.017, L 0.018). The criterion asks for four rats at p < 0.01, or three for a partial reproduction, so the outcome is not reproduced; at p < 0.05 four rats (E, J, K, L) would hold, which is the pattern the legend reports with p < 0.01. The sign tests hold as the legend says at 10 cm, the initial ratio above 2 and the final below 2 with p < 0.05 in E, J, K and L and not in M. Days with no same-side transition are dropped, as the criterion says (1 day of E and 2 of J for the initial ratio). In a variant asked for by the verifier, adding one to both counts so that no day is dropped, J, K and L reach p < 0.01 and E has p = 0.010; that would be a partial reproduction, but the criterion's rule decides.
deviations: The previous trial is the one before in the same session, and transitions from the previous arm to the same arm are left out as neither switch-side nor same-side; the claims file does not say.
Sessions with fewer than 20 trials are left out (claims file, opening comment, point 2).

outcomes.notes: Sessions with at least 20 trials. The sign test of the daily final-choice ratios against 1 gives p = 0.38, 0.18, 1.0, 0.45 and 0.22 for M, E, J, K and L, so no rat differs; the median ratios are 1.29, 1.33, 1.00, 0.93 and 1.41. For rat M (5 days) the test cannot reach p < 0.05 (smallest two-sided p 0.0625), so this is a weak absence result there.

outcomes.notes: COM rows are the 908 rows of the 160 COM-triggered, arm-restricted tables from arm entry to stopping (in a median 90% of rows per file the trigger lies within 20 ms of one of this entry's COM times, at a median distance of 2 ms); 896 have a distance. Controls are the 975 rows of the 177 tables triggered at the outer poke, 2 s before it (outbound runs), restricted to the arm; 737 have a distance over a head range drawn from the same day's COM rows. Largest |head - decode| at 4 cm/s or more, COM against matched control: medians 13.8 against 10.0 cm (M), 12.7 against 12.5 (E), 15.8 against 13.6 (J), 19.3 against 13.1 (K) and 16.4 against 13.0 (L); one-sided rank-sum p < 1e-4, 0.053, 0.0072, < 1e-4 and < 1e-4. So COM is greater at p < 0.01 in 4 of 5 rats (not E). Only reading (b)(i) can be run: the arm-restricted tables set moments with 0.2 or less of the posterior in the arm to NaN, and the control tables hold only the 2 s before the poke, not 5 s. Without matching the arm range the controls have larger distances (p = 1.0 in all five rats). The arm range of each control row is one random draw, as in the code, and the outcome depends on it. Over 20 further draws, each with its own seed, all five rats hold in 11 draws, four in 8 and three in 1 (E and J each fail in 5), and the median p over the draws is below 0.01 in every rat (E 0.007, J 0.0045). Adding to the COM rows the 48 rows of the arm-restricted tables before stopping that match neither trigger (14 of E, 23 of J), three rats hold in the first draw (E p = 0.088, J 0.013), and over the further draws five rats hold in 3, four in 11 and three in 6 (median p for E 0.014). With all of the paper's COM tables the result is partial in most draws, so the outcome is kept.

One-sided rank-sum, COM greater: under the smaller decode bound p = 3e-8, 0.041, 0.062, 8e-15 and 8e-9 for M, E, J, K and L (3 rats at p < 0.0001, 4 at p < 0.05, the partial bar); under the larger bound p = 9e-14, 5e-10, 0.008, 7e-20 and 8e-14 (4 rats at p < 0.0001, the full bar). The two-sided variant gives 3 rats at p < 0.0001 under the smaller bound (and 3 at p < 0.05) and 4 under the larger. The outcome verified in round 2 rested on the smaller bound. Round 2 identified the decoder: every arm-restricted table, the inbound ones among them, has the decodes of one decoder (A; 353 pairs of arm-restricted tables sharing samples all agree), and the code takes the COM and control decodes of a figure from one decoder. Under decoder A, p = 2e-8, 0.053, 0.064, 1e-16 and 9e-9 (3 rats at p < 0.0001 and 3 at p < 0.05, below the partial bar). outcomes.notes: Remote events need the decoder's posterior per 2 ms bin over each COM event and its continuous-state probability, which the dandiset does not hold; the triggered tables hold only the MAP position in windows around COM times and outer pokes. They would have to be recomputed by spike detection and clusterless state-space decoding of every run session from the 30 kHz voltage, 12.5 TB of raw files over the 40 days (313 GB per day on average); streaming alone at the rate the notebook measures on an LFP file (62 to 72 MB/s over the runs of this revision) would take about 2 days.

Measured values are window a, reading (ii), the first matching reading the criterion lists, without the reference subtraction. SWRs detected on the 1 kHz LFP of 39 days (rat M's fifth day has no LFP file; 64 of 2706 windows dropped). Per rat, as many unrewarded and rewarded trial ends as COM trials (120, 196, 124, 223, 239). Under reading (iii), the pseudo-inverse fit with a constant, all rat indicators and the three conditions, the COM coefficient is negative and both end coefficients positive with p < 0.05 in both windows and both reference readings (window a, no subtraction, -0.043, 0.049 and 0.030 events/s, p = 6e-12, 3e-15 and 1e-6). Reading (ii), z-scored within rat, holds without the subtraction in both windows (window a -0.22, 0.15 and 0.07; the rewarded value is outside 0.30 plus or minus 0.16) and not with it; reading (i), the three conditions without a constant, holds in none. The mean COM rate is below both end rates in 5 of 5 rats in window a without the subtraction and in 4 of 5 otherwise. Ripples are rare: 0.13 to 0.34 per second of immobility in the baseline windows and at most 0.22 per second at trial ends. The LFP shares the behavioral clock: theta amplitude correlates with head speed at no shift (median Spearman 0.68 over 13 days) and not at shifts of 5 or 30 s (-0.20 to -0.02), weakly in rat K. Against the paper's coefficients (-0.18, 0.22 and 0.30), the z-scored reading gives a COM coefficient of larger magnitude and smaller end-of-trial coefficients. With one rat left out, reading (iii) holds in every fit without the subtraction; with the subtraction it holds with any of M, E, J or L left out and fails without rat K (window a, COM -0.0009, p = 0.62; window b, unrewarded end -0.011), so with the subtraction the result rests on rat K, which has no reference channel in its files. The outcome stands on the reading without the subtraction, which holds with any rat left out.

findings.statement: The decoder output behind Figures 4, 5 and S3 to S11 (the posterior per 2 ms bin over whole sessions, the continuous and fragmented state probabilities, the detected remote and local extended events) is not deposited, nor are the spike marks or MUA times. The triggered tables hold only the MAP position in windows around COM times and outer pokes. The rest would have to be recomputed from the raw voltage, 12.5 TB of raw files.

None of the 2415 Spyglass analysis files (`obj-*.nwb`) says what it holds; the file names carry only an object id, and their tables have empty descriptions. By content they are head position, velocity and orientation (750), linearized position at about 23 Hz and at 500 Hz (446), and decodes triggered on events (1219). The triggered tables could be read only with the paper's code and by aligning their trigger times with COM times and outer pokes: 720 are triggered at COM times, 353 at outer pokes, and 146 at times that match neither. The parameters that made each (trigger, window, restriction to the arm, MAP or mean, which decoder) are in the lab's database, not the files; the whole-track tables come in pairs with different decodes, and which decoder made each can be told only from which member agrees with the arm-restricted tables, not named. The track graph of the linearization is not deposited.

The dandiset holds fewer trials than the paper reports for three rats. Built from the poke and pump events, it holds 2083, 3519, 4578, 2959 and 1816 trials for rats M, E, J, K and L, against 2370, 3554, 4628, 3779 and 2087 in the Figure 1E inset (0.88, 0.99, 0.99, 0.78 and 0.87 of them). Rat M has 5 days against the 6 the paper says were collected; rat J has 12 days against about 11 in Figure 1C. Rat M's 5 days of about 400 trials would account for its shortfall; rats K and L have the days of Figure 1C, and no epoch is tagged other than Session or Sleep, so where their trials are missing is not known.
Rat M's 500 Hz linearizations are each deposited twice, in 26 pairs of files with identical values, one pair per run epoch. They are counted once.

Rat M's Statescript logs are named "syayescript Seq2Session1" and so on, a misspelling of "statescript", and hold no trial or reward counts, unlike the other rats' logs. Rat M's days also have 4 LFP files for 5 days.

The reward log gives the cycle 3-4-2-1-3 for rats M, E and J and 1-2-4-3-1 for rats K and L. This fits the Results (1-2-4-3-1 in 2 rats, 3-4-2-1-3 in 3) and the Figure 1B legend (rat E, 3-4-2-1-3), while Figure S1E labels Seq2 (1-2-4-3-1) for M, E and J. The files name the epochs of K and L "Rev2" and those of M, E and J "Seq2".
The head orientation series (`scratch/CompassDirection/head_orientation`) gives its unit as meters.

The electrode table of the LFP files has no locations, so the CA1 tetrodes and the corpus callosum reference used for ripple detection (Methods, SWR detection) cannot be identified; the reference named by `ref_elect_id` is in the LFP file on some days only (never for rat K).
The LFP series (`scratch/filtered data`) gives its unit as volts with a conversion of 1.0, while the data are int16 values with a standard deviation of about 240.

For Figure 3D, which decoder (run_time or all_maze) made the whole-track tables the paper used, and which made the arm-restricted tables? The deposited whole-track tables come in pairs with different decodes; one member of each pair (A) agrees with every arm-restricted table. Under A the claim is at the edge of its partial bar (3 or 4 rats at p < 0.05 depending on the random draw of arm ranges), under the other decoder it holds in full (4 rats at p < 0.0001). Which tables around COM time entered Figure 3 (146 tables have rows mostly not at this attempt''s COM times) is also not said.

For Figure S7B, which tetrodes and which reference channel entered SWR detection, and over what period was the session baseline taken? This attempt used every tetrode of the LFP file, the `ref_elect_id` channel where present or none, and 20 sampled windows per run epoch; ripples came out rare (0.13 to 0.34 per second of immobility).

entries.name: 001836-gu-2026
entries.title: Change-of-mind behavior in the spatial sequence task (Gu et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the behavioral findings of Gu, Liu, Gillespie, Nevers, Denovellis, Coulter, Kay and Frank (2026) on dandiset 001836, which holds the recordings of five rats learning a hidden four-arm sequence. It builds trials from the well pokes and pumps, detects change-of-mind trials on the deposited linearized position, and tests learning, side-switching bias, trial counts and the corrective effect of changes of mind. It reads the paper's triggered decode tables for the Figure 3 claims and detects ripples on the LFP for Figure S7B; the other claims on hippocampal content need the decoder output, which the dandiset does not hold.
